summary: Solar System Adventure is an interactive 3D web platform designed to teach children about our Solar System and NASA's robotic space missions. By clicking on 3D planets, kids trigger smooth camera zooms and playful speech bubbles featuring kid-friendly stories and real NASA imagery of spacecraft like Perseverance, Juno, and Cassini.
details:
Solar System Adventure is an interactive, 3D educational web platform designed specifically to introduce children to the Solar System and NASA's robotic space exploration missions in a fun, visual, and accessible way.
How It Works & Key Features:
Upon entering the website, children are greeted by a dynamic 3D model of our Solar System. By simply clicking on any planet, the camera smoothly zooms in and tracks that planet while a colorful, kid-friendly speech bubble appears on the screen. This bubble presents engaging stories and real images of the NASA spacecraft (such as Perseverance, Juno, and Cassini) that have explored that world, translating complex space science into simple, exciting concepts.
Benefits & Intended Impact:
Traditional space textbooks and static articles can feel overwhelming for young learners. The primary impact of Solar System Adventure is to spark early curiosity in STEM, astronomy, and space engineering by turning passive reading into active exploration. By connecting each planet with the human-made robots visiting them, children learn not only about planets, but also how NASA explores the universe.
Tools, Technologies & AI Disclosure:
As a solo participant, I designed the educational concept, user experience, and NASA spacecraft content curation myself. To bring the 3D vision to life within the hackathon timeframe, I utilized AI-assisted web development tools (Lovable) to generate a web application built on Three.js (WebGL), React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS. All scientific information and spacecraft visuals were sourced from official NASA archives (NASA Solar System Exploration and NASA Image and Video Library).
Creativity & Design Considerations:
Instead of building a standard text-heavy website, I focused on spatial storytelling—combining smooth 3D camera zoom mechanics with playful, clutter-free UI speech bubbles tailored for young eyes. Key factors considered during development included intuitive navigation without complex menus, high visual contrast against a dark space background, and age-appropriate storytelling that keeps children engaged from the very first click.
